messages.content: You read a software project description and fill in questionnaire answers. Rules: (1) Include a question only when the text states or clearly implies the answer; never guess and never use defaults. (2) For every value give a short "quote" copied word for word from the text that supports it. (3) Use only the allowed values listed for each question. (4) Fill a question only from words that describe THAT question's subject. A sentence about the team's skills (who knows which language or database) says nothing about the data, the traffic, the platforms or the budget, so never take a data shape, a scale or a requirement from it; use it only for team skills. Reply with one JSON object: {"fields": {"<key>": {"value": <value>, "quote": "<words from the text>"}}}. Reply with {"fields": {}} when nothing qualifies.

Questions you may answer:
- "app_type": one of "saas", "ecommerce", "realtime_collab", "content_site", "analytics_dashboard", "ml_product", "iot_telemetry", "fintech", "healthcare", "social_network", "internal_tool", "mobile_first", "prototype". Application type: The workload archetype sets default traffic shape, data model hints and which criteria matter (e.g. SEO for content, consistency for fintech).
- "user_actions": a list of any of "read", "sign_in", "post", "pay". What do users do?: If users only read (no sign-in, no posting, no payments), the site can be static files on a CDN: no database server and no API code to run.
- "special_workloads": a list of any of "media_uploads", "video_on_demand", "text_search", "live_video", "live_location", "phone_otp", "user_code". Special workloads: Each one adds a specialised service the four main picks do not cover, usually billed by use: video minutes, map loads, SMS messages or data served (egress).
- "peak_rps": a number from 0 to 10000000. Peak requests per second (optional): Leave blank to derive it: DAU x requests-per-user-per-day (by app type) / 86,400 x a peak factor by app type (10 e-commerce, 6 social, 3 content sites, 1.5 IoT, 5 otherwise).
- "traffic_pattern": one of "auto", "steady", "spiky". Traffic pattern: Sets how far the busiest second is above the average second. Only used when you do not enter a peak RPS.
- "cacheable_share": one of "auto", "little", "some", "most". How much of the traffic can be cached?: Cached requests are served by a CDN or memory and never reach the server or database. This also scales a peak RPS you enter yourself.
- "data_volume_gb": a number from 0 to 100000000. Data volume at launch: Primary database size, excluding media files (those go to object storage).
- "data_growth_gb_month": a number from 0 to 10000000. Data growth per month: Used to project 12-month volume.
- "read_write": one of "read_heavy", "balanced", "write_heavy". Read / write mix: Read-heavy workloads benefit from caches and replicas; write-heavy ones from LSM/wide-column or time-series engines.
- "data_shapes": a list of any of "relational", "document", "key_value", "time_series", "graph", "analytical", "vector", "search". Data shape (first = primary): The first selection is weighted double. Secondary shapes may be served by a supporting datastore.
- "consistency": one of "strong", "eventual_ok". Consistency requirement: Strong consistency excludes eventually-consistent stores as the system of record.
- "realtime": one of "none", "some", "core". Realtime needs: Core realtime requires persistent connections (WebSockets). Static/CDN hosts cannot hold them, and on serverless platforms support is limited or new (Vercel Functions added WebSockets in beta), so long-running servers score higher.
- "latency_target_ms": a number from 5 to 60000. p95 API latency target: 100 ms feels instant; 1 s keeps flow of thought (Nielsen).
- "seo": one of "none", "important", "critical". Search engine visibility: SEO favours server-rendered or static HTML frameworks.
- "offline": true or false. Offline support required: Field apps, rural connectivity, mobile-first markets.
- "availability": one of "99.0", "99.9", "99.95", "99.99". Availability target: Each extra nine roughly needs another layer of redundancy (multi-AZ, then multi-region).
- "regions": a list of any of "india", "southeast_asia", "europe", "north_america", "global". Where are your users?: Hosting without a nearby region adds round-trip latency (e.g. Singapore to Mumbai is ~60 ms).
- "team_size": a number from 1 to 5000. Engineering team size: People writing and operating the software in the first year.
- "timeline_weeks": a number from 1 to 520. Time to MVP: Calendar weeks until first real users.
- "architecture": one of "auto", "monolith", "microservices", "serverless". Architecture preference: Microservices with fewer than ~3 engineers per service is flagged as a risk.
- "deployment": one of "cloud", "hybrid", "on_prem". Deployment model: On-prem excludes managed-only services (Vercel, Lambda, DynamoDB, Firestore, Firebase).
- "cloud_preference": one of "none", "aws", "gcp", "azure". Preferred cloud: Existing credits, contracts or skills. Applied as a strong preference, not a hard filter.
- "lock_in_tolerance": one of "low", "medium", "high". Vendor lock-in tolerance: Low tolerance removes highly proprietary services (Firebase, DynamoDB, Firestore) unless nothing else fits.
- "compliance": a list of any of "gdpr", "dpdp", "hipaa", "pci_dss", "soc2", "data_residency_india", "data_residency_eu". Compliance & data residency: HIPAA requires a signed BAA with every vendor touching PHI; residency requires an in-country region.
- "priorities": a list of any of "cost", "speed", "scale", "performance", "low_ops", "proven". Your top 3 priorities (first = most important): Optional. The first pick gets the biggest extra weight, then the second, then the third. Leave empty to use no extra weight.
- "existing_systems": a list of any of "postgres", "mysql", "mongodb", "redis", "sqlserver", "oracle". Existing systems you must keep: Databases your company already runs. A listed database StackSense knows gets a strong bonus; one it does not know is flagged instead.
